notes: Which language is R1, R2 and R3 is the founders' decision: here English→R1 (foundational CG-10 'Language 1' rows for G1–G2), Hindi→R2 (foundational CG-11 'Language 2' rows for G1–G2), Marathi→R2 for its content units and R3 for its Grade-4 script units; every id can be re-pointed wholesale.

NCF has no preparatory-stage R3 rows (a third language starts at Grade 6) and no R2 row for beginning a script after Grade 2, so the 14 Grade-4 Marathi script units (मुळाक्षरे, स्वरचिन्ह, सोळाखडी, जोडाक्षरे, अंकलेखन) sit on r3.S.C-5.1 (script and phonetics) and r3.M.C-2.1 (reading words) by text, two stages above the children; if Marathi becomes R2, re-point them to r2.P.C-2.1 and C-2.2.

The NCERT file holds English outcomes only, so every R2 and R3 row has an empty ncert list (NCERT's Hindi outcomes and Maharashtra's Marathi ones would fill them), and five R1 rows have no NCERT outcome at all: r1.P.C-5.1 library borrowing, r1.M.C-1.5 audio-visual content, r1.M.C-5.1 the phonetics and script of English, r1.S.C-4.3 language and identity, r1.S.C-4.5 tribal and regional languages.

NCERT keeps assessing reading aloud with pause and intonation up to class 10 (eng 3.03, 4.12, 7.02, 9.06) while NCF places fluency only at the foundational stage (fnd C-10.4), and R1 has no grammar, vocabulary, conversation or oral-presentation row after the preparatory stage, so some class 6–10 outcomes point at foundational or preparatory rows (fnd C-10.4; r1.P.C-1.1, C-1.3, C-4.1) and class 9–10 grammar at r1.M.C-3.1.

The school's G2 English (Roald Dahl novels, letters and emails, playscripts, book reviews) and G1–G2 Hindi (paragraph, dialogue and letter writing) run a stage ahead of the foundational rows they are mapped to; Play-Based Learning (units 062, 229, 377) and NCERT's language-lab visits, Sign Language and Braille outcomes are left empty with a why.
